description: City of Pasadena, Texas Ordinance 2025-082 (adopted April 1, 2025), adding Article XII, Energy Storage Systems, to Chapter 9 of the Code of Ordinances as a land use code: battery energy storage (BESS) sites are capped at five acres, kept 500 feet from residential property, 1,000 feet from critical facilities and 1,500 feet from another BESS site, must be located within 150 feet of Centerpoint Energy property, may not be in a special flood hazard area, and require a special use permit.
mechanisms: setback, cap on acreage, zoning restriction
long_description: BESS site no larger than five (5) acres, measured property line to property line (Sec. 9-225(a)); BESS site no closer than 500 feet, measured from the nearest property line, to residential property, platted residential property or platted residential subdivision, and to multifamily developments or manufactured home parks (Sec. 9-225(d)); no closer than 1,000 feet to all critical facilities (defined to include hospitals and health care facilities, nursing homes, schools, day care centers, police and fire stations, government facilities and public or private utility facilities), excluding other BESS sites and Centerpoint Energy facilities, measured from the nearest property line (Sec. 9-225(e)); no closer than 1,500 feet to another BESS site, measured from nearest property line (Sec. 9-225(b)); location rule: BESS site must be located within 150 feet of a Centerpoint Energy transfer station or Centerpoint Energy owned property or fee strip (Sec. 9-225(c)); BESS site may not be located in a special flood hazard area (Sec. 9-225(g)); structures, buildings and equipment set back 50 feet from the right of way and 150 feet from rear and side property lines adjacent to commercial property (Sec. 9-225(f)); a Special Use Permit application is required (Sec. 9-224(d)).
notes: Queued 2026-10-16 as a lead from the renewables case-study review (deliverables/case_study_templates/renewables_2026-10-16, pricephillips/renewable-opposition#61), where it was found in passing; not triaged. The review read the ordinance text in the March 18, 2025 agenda packet and its adoption in the April 1, 2025 minutes, https://www.pasadenatx.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_04012025-574 ; it reported a five-acre cap, 500 feet from residential property, 1,000 feet from critical facilities, 1,500 feet between sites, a site within 150 feet of utility property, no mapped flood zones, and a special use permit. Triaged 2026-10-16 by agent:lead-triager-2 (Claude Code, 2026-10-16): Read the Article XII text in the March 18, 2025 agenda backup (a scan; its OCR layer was checked against the page images of pp. 748, 753, 755 and 760 to 762) and the minutes of March 18 (passed on first reading only) and April 1, 2025 (Ordinance 2025-082 passed on second and final reading); the ordinance calls itself a land use code and sets siting rules beyond fire and building clearances (5-acre cap, 500 ft from residential property, 1,000 ft from critical facilities, 1,500 ft between BESS sites, a site within 150 ft of Centerpoint Energy property, no special flood hazard area, a special use permit), every figure the review reported matches, and it is a separate instrument from the 2024 moratorium (mn:tx-pasadena-2024), which it does not name. The packet copy is the unnumbered first-reading draft and neither set of minutes records an amendment, but the adopted or codified text was not seen (Municode returned 403 and the April 1 backup does not re-attach the ordinance), so the adopted text could differ; status active rests on final passage and the absence of any sunset clause, and no effective date is stated. Reviewed 2026-10-16 by agent:blind-reviewer-2 (Claude Code, 2026-10-16): confirmed. Read the City of Pasadena March 18, 2025 council agenda packet (883 scanned pages; pages 748 to 766 hold the agenda request and the unnumbered ordinance with Exhibit A, Article XII, Energy Storage Systems; quotes are from the rendered page images because the scanner text layer has OCR errors) and the April 1, 2025 council minutes (https://www.pasadenatx.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_04012025-574, opened), which record Ordinance 2025-082 under the same caption passed on second and final reading, unanimous, at a meeting of the City of Pasadena, Harris County, Texas. The article sits in Chapter 9 (Buildings) but is adopted as a land use code to designate properties suitable for BESS, and Sec. 9-225 sets a 5-acre site cap, 500 ft from residential property, 1,000 ft from critical facilities, 1,500 ft between BESS sites, a site within 150 ft of CenterPoint property and no special flood hazard area, with a special use permit under Sec. 9-224: siting rules under COUNTY_CHECK section 3, not fire or building code clearances. It applies to all ESS permitted after it takes effect (consumer-product batteries, 12-volt car batteries and vehicles are excluded), so it reaches utility-scale BESS. Status active rests on final passage and the absence of any sunset clause; the codified code on Municode returned a Cloudflare challenge, so a later amendment was not checked. The ordinance states no separate effective date. The published record mn:tx-pasadena-2024 is the city's BESS permit moratorium, a different instrument, so this lead is not its duplicate; the review queue itself was not searched (outside this lane). The 500 ft distance is the one from homes; 1,500 ft is the spacing between BESS sites, which the build's largest-distance rule would read as the setback. Noted 2026-10-16 by agent:case-study-drafter-1 (Claude Code, 2026-10-16): Possible repeal, not yet checked: the City Council agenda backup for October 7, 2025 (https://www.pasadenatx.gov/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_10072025-629, opened 2026-10-16 by agent:blind-reviewer-8 and agent:qc-auditor-3) carries a proposed ordinance adopting the 2024 International Fire Code, captioned 'repealing Ordinance 2025-082 adopted on April 1, 2025', whose Section 3 reads 'That Ordinance 2025-082, previously adopted by Council on April 1, 2025 is hereby repealed.' and which moves the energy storage requirements into the fire code. No minutes showing whether it passed were found (none are posted for October 2025). Status active needs re-reading against that ordinance's fate.
